Bill.BriefDescription: Concerning a sales and use tax exemption for restaurants in respect to certain items that impart flavor to food during the cooking process.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to a sales and use tax exemption for restaurants inrespect to certain items that impart flavor to food during the cookingprocess; adding a new section to chapter 82.08 RCW; adding a newsection to chapter 82.12 RCW; and providing an effective date.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 82.08 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Except as provided in subsection (2) of this section, the taxlevied by RCW 82.08.020 does not apply to sales to restaurants ofproducts that impart flavor to food during the cooking process andthat: (a) Are completely or substantially consumed by combustion duringthe cooking process, such as wood chips, charcoal, charcoal briquettes,and grape vines; or (b) Support the food during the cooking process and are comprisedentirely of wood, such as cedar grilling planks. (2) The exemption provided by this section does not apply to anytype of gas fuel. p. 1 SB 5342 (3) Sellers making taxexempt sales under this section must obtainan exemption certificate from the buyer in a form and manner prescribedby the department. The seller must retain a copy of the exemptioncertificate for the seller's files. In lieu of an exemptioncertificate, a seller may capture the relevant data elements as allowedunder the streamlined sales and use tax agreement. (4) For purposes of this subsection, "restaurant" has the samemeaning as provided in RCW 82.08.9995.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 82.12 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Except as provided in subsection (2) of this section, theprovisions of this chapter do not apply to restaurants with respect tothe use of products that impart flavor to food during the cookingprocess and that: (a) Are completely or substantially consumed by combustion duringthe cooking process, such as wood chips, charcoal, charcoal briquettes,and grape vines; or (b) Support the food during the cooking process and are comprisedentirely of wood, such as cedar grilling planks. (2) The exemption provided by this section does not apply to anytype of gas fuel. (3) For purposes of this subsection, "restaurant" has the samemeaning as provided in RCW 82.08.9995.
